stator.name: Stator and frame
stator.does: The finned frame with its feet holds the stator core and its three-phase winding; the rotating field the winding makes turns the rotor. Cooled from outside by the fan's air over the fins (IC 411).
stator.material: Cast iron frame, laminated electrical steel core, copper winding

terminal_box.name: Terminal box
terminal_box.does: Where the supply cable lands on the winding's terminals U1, V1, W1; record the connections before it is opened.

end_shield_de.name: Drive-end shield
end_shield_de.does: Closes the frame at the drive end and holds the drive-end bearing in its housing; its bearing cap keeps the grease in.

end_shield_nde.name: Non-drive-end shield
end_shield_nde.does: Closes the frame at the fan end and holds the non-drive-end bearing in its housing.

fan.name: Cooling fan
fan.does: On the shaft's non-drive end: blows air along the frame's fins whichever way the motor turns (straight radial blades). A fan fitted with interference is replaced, not reused.

fan_cowl.name: Fan cowl
fan_cowl.does: Guards the fan and guides its air over the fins.
fan_cowl.sealed_why: The grille is part of the fan cowl: they come off as one.

grille.name: Air intake grille
grille.does: Lets the cooling air in at the cowl's end; kept clear of dirt.

rotor.name: Rotor
rotor.does: The squirrel-cage rotor on its shaft: the stator's field drives it round. Drawn out of the stator's bore without touching the winding.
rotor.material: Laminated steel core, aluminium cage, steel shaft

bearing_de.name: Drive-end bearing
bearing_de.does: A rolling bearing on the shaft at the drive end, in the drive-end shield: it carries the load the coupling puts on the shaft.

bearing_nde.name: Non-drive-end bearing
bearing_nde.does: A rolling bearing on the shaft at the fan end, in the non-drive-end shield.

baseplate.name: Baseplate
baseplate.does: The steel frame the motor's feet are bolted to, grouted to the floor.

text: The baseplate stays grouted to the floor.
Set the stator in its frame on its baseplate, feet down, the winding protected.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

The baseplate stays grouted to the floor.

text: Slide the rotor into the stator's bore from the drive end, its weight carried so that it never rests on the winding.
why: A rotor dragged against the winding damages its insulation. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: stator
The rotor goes into the stator's bore: set the stator down first.
Draw the rotor out before the stator is moved.

text: Fit the drive-end bearing on the shaft, heated, pressing on its inner ring only.
why: In the shop the bearings go on the shaft before the rotor goes in, and come off it once the rotor is out (in the steps here they are fitted and taken off in place). Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: Fit the non-drive-end bearing on the shaft the same way.

text: Fit the non-drive-end shield over its bearing and into the frame, with its bearing cap.
why: Its spigot is entered square, without forcing, so that the bearing is not loaded. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

The shield's housing closes over the non-drive-end bearing: fit the bearing first.
Take the non-drive-end shield off before its bearing.

The shield's housing closes over the drive-end bearing: fit the bearing first.

text: Fit the four drive-end shield bolts and tighten them evenly; turn the shaft by hand: it must turn freely.

text: Push the fan onto the shaft's non-drive end and lock it.

The fan sits behind the non-drive-end shield: fit the shield first.
Pull the fan off before the non-drive-end shield comes off.
